name: Prize crossword No 21,963
preamble: Method: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise. Because the grid is symmetrical, there are two possible ways of filling it in; the correct way displays the compass points (especially North) on the perimeter.

clue.text: Spooner's desire, Scots county, I could swear

definitions.note: a self-description: the speaker is the foul-mouthed woman, so it stands for a noun

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the two words that follow get their starts exchanged

blocks.note: desire is a wish and Fife a Scottish county; say the pair with their opening sounds swapped

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a corner of Scotland so badly they could curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Wish Fife, with the first sounds swapped, becomes FISH WIFE. Fishwives selling at market were famous for coarse language.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife is proverbially a loud, coarse-tongued woman, exactly the kind of person who might boast of swearing.

clue.text: This aromatic oil the Rand supplied

indicators.note: read as 'made supple', the word before it is bent into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African gold-mining region is said to be the source of a perfumed oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rand is the Witwatersrand gold field near Johannesburg; 'supplied' looks like a verb of trade but signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nard, or spikenard, is a fragrant ointment prepared from a Himalayan plant, prized in ancient times.

clue.text: Some stop a question to conceal the truth

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the phrase describes what opaque language does

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words after dropping the first two and the last five

explanation.surface: A politician blocks a question to cover up what really happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque speech is deliberately obscure, letting no light through, so it serves to hide what is really going on.

clue.text: Touching one pound, first lady mollify

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
the Roman numeral for one
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A first lady is soothed by being handed a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound comes before the one in the answer, though the clue lists them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve pain or anxiety is to ease or soften it, the same calming sense as mollify.

clue.text: Some current in some trade: I interfere

definitions.note: self-description standing for a noun: one who interferes

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of it is kept, here its opening pair of letters
in places one piece inside the remains of the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut down to its first two letters
the ampere is the unit in which electric current is measured

explanation.surface: An electrician meddling in a business admits to interfering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some trade' and 'Some current' both mean a portion: a bit of the word, and a quantity of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamperer is someone who meddles with things they should leave alone, which is what the speaker confesses.

clue.text: Man's genus, nous A1, formed faith Nicene

definitions.note: the answer names the believer or doctrine; the inverted order serves the surface

indicators.note: formed suggests material shaped into something new, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Homo is the biological genus that includes humans
taken as written, with 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Human intelligence of the first rate shaped the creed agreed at Nicaea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nicene Creed of 325 declared the Son to be of the same substance as the Father, homoousios in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Homoousian is the term for the Nicene doctrine, or its holder, that Father and Son share one identical essence.

clue.text: Sets of adults, with void where heart has been

indicators.text: with void where heart has been
indicators.note: an empty space where the heart was means the central letters are taken out

blocks.note: grown-ups are adults

explanation.surface: Groups of adults are described as hollow-hearted, as if the grown-ups had lost their feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters, here W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets and groups are both collections of things or people classed together.

clue.text: Is this the fruit first lady's tempted by?

definitions.text: Is this the fruit first lady's tempted by?

blocks.clueFragment: Is this the fruit first lady's tempted by?
blocks.note: surface reading: Eve in Eden being lured by the forbidden fruit
setter's reading: the city nickname for New York, which might tempt a president's wife to visit

explanation.surface: A question about which fruit Eve could not resist in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: First lady suggests Eve, but it can also mean a US president's wife, for whom the great city is a lure.
explanation.definitionFit: New York City is nicknamed after an outsized piece of fruit, which ties neatly to Eve's temptation.

clue.text: In craft commercial keeping king in sty

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial on TV or radio
the male pig is lord of the pigsty

explanation.surface: A cunning advert features a pig ruling its sty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King in sty' is not R in a word; it is a playful description of the male pig.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on or in a ship, aircraft or other vessel.

clue.text: Abandoned building: silence pressman here

blocks.note: sh is the call for silence
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: In a derelict building someone hushes a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: two meanings plus a charade built from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to cast off or discard, and a shed is a simple outbuilding for storage.

clue.text: A swap, perhaps, for what a pound will buy

blocks.note: a quid is slang for one pound sterling
Latin pro means for
Latin quo, the ablative of quod, means what

explanation.surface: A trade-in is described as whatever a pound coin can purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'something for something', and the clue renders it word by word as 'for what a pound'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid pro quo is a favour or item given in exchange for another, so it is a kind of swap.

clue.text: I'm typecast close to Durham: I need Ruth!

indicators.note: cast suggests something thrown or moulded afresh, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of I'm and type, taken as written; the last four letters of the word are the signal

explanation.surface: A typecast actor near Durham begs for a woman named Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth is an old word for pity or compassion, so 'I need Ruth!' is a cry for sympathy. Pity Me is a village just north of Durham in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The village name is also the plea of someone wanting compassion, and ruth is an archaic noun for that feeling.

clue.text: It's moved by oar (not nice) or hand (not good)

indicators.note: moved letters are shifted out of their order, so the following pair are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
rough means harsh or unpleasant

explanation.surface: Something is propelled either by rowing or by hand, with grumbles about each.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed asides look like comments on the oar and the hand; one is wordplay and the other completes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In whist and bridge a yarborough is a dealt hand with no card higher than a nine, named after an earl who bet against it.

clue.text: Skilled man or one from Rome turned out like this

indicators.note: turned suggests being twisted round into a different order, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: vir is the Latin word for a man
taken as written
so means in this way

explanation.surface: A clever man, or perhaps a Roman, has ended up this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skilled man' looks like the definition, but man belongs with 'one from Rome' to give the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Used attributively, as in a virtuoso performance, the word describes dazzling technical mastery.

clue.text: Cunning grips listener as his hard day ends

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase describing manner, matching the adverb answer

indicators.note: to grip is to hold tightly, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: wily means crafty or cunning
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A sly person buttonholes someone willing to hear him out at the end of a tough day.
explanation.definitionFit: At the close of a hard day a person moves in a tired, exhausted manner.

clue.text: The field is by the railway, which is tough

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word for a field
taken as written
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A farmer complains that his field next to the railway line is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: The field comes before the word 'The' in the answer, the reverse of their order in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leathery is hard and chewy, with the toughness of tanned hide.

clue.text: Ailsa - that's Jill, the Labour leader's wife

blocks.note: Ailsa Craig is a rocky island in the Firth of Clyde, so Ailsa suggests its partner word
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone named Ailsa is identified as the wife of a Labour Party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Ailsa looks like a woman's name to set against Jill; here it is half of an island's name. Ailsa Craig is a small granite island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Jill Craigie, a film-maker and writer, was married to Michael Foot, who led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983.

clue.text: Bad moment? Something wrong with judge's watch?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the noun phrase describes a moment that is ill-timed
the answer is an adjective; the phrase describes a timepiece badly regulated

blocks.note: first meaning: coming at an inconvenient, inopportune time
second meaning, read literally: a watch whose timing has gone wrong, perhaps the one a judge uses at a race

explanation.surface: An awkward moment as the official timekeeper's stopwatch seems faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into its parts: ill, meaning badly, and timed, meaning measured by a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-timed means done at an unsuitable moment, and also, taken literally, poorly measured against a clock.

clue.text: God 'olds 'is 'eadlight, doing all one could

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the phrase describes a zealous person's effort

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in this cockney word shows the next word must also lose its opening H
holds, with its aitch dropped, means one piece contains the other

blocks.note: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods
a halo is the ring of light round a saint's head, then said without its aitch

explanation.surface: A cockney describes a god holding his headlight while giving it his all.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes show cockney dropped aitches, telling the solver to drop the H from the halo too.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous means full of eager devotion, putting every possible effort into a cause.

clue.text: Fire school in time: give, holding alien life

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out at a school just in time while someone donates to aliens.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue gives the answer a second way: donate (give) holding ET, the film alien, also makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire a charge or explosive is to set it off, which is what detonate means.

clue.text: The cricket team has time for cafetière

definitions.note: the hour of the mid-morning coffee break

blocks.note: first meaning: a cricket side has this many players
second meaning: the morning hour of the coffee break called elevenses

explanation.surface: The cricketers stop for a pot of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: A cafetière is a plunger coffee pot; the British call a mid-morning snack elevenses after the hour it is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side is called an eleven, and eleven o'clock is traditional coffee time in Britain.

clue.text: One writer's tales and books, precise hotchpotch

definitions.note: Kipling's Jungle Books; the answer is the first word of their title

blocks.note: first meaning: the ... Books by Rudyard Kipling, the writer named in the shared clue
second meaning: a tangled confusion or muddle
surface padding here: this word belongs to the companion entry sharing the clue

explanation.surface: An author's collected stories and volumes make an exact jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: One clue serves two entries: Kipling wrote both the Just So Stories and The Jungle Book, and each title's first part also means something on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A jungle can mean any confused, chaotic tangle, so it matches a hotchpotch or jumble of things.

clue.text: One writer's tales and books, precise hotchpotch

definitions.note: Kipling's Just So Stories; the answer is the start of the title

blocks.note: first meaning: the stories for children by Rudyard Kipling
second meaning: exactly right, arranged with care
surface padding here: this word belongs to the companion entry sharing the clue
surface padding here: this word belongs to the companion entry sharing the clue

explanation.surface: An author's collected stories and volumes make an exact jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: One clue serves two entries; this one takes the tales and the word precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Things arranged with fussy exactness are said to be neatly in order, and the phrase means exactly that.

clue.text: One turned in weird tales heard by aliens? friends

indicators.note: turned means the word is read in the opposite direction
in places one piece inside the other
heard means we want what the title sounds like, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: The X-Files was a TV series of weird, paranormal tales
taken as written

explanation.surface: Strange stories are listened to by visitors from outer space, who are friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: The suffix -philes means lovers of, and sounds just like the files of the TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophiles are people attracted to foreigners or strangers, so they are friends to aliens in the earthly sense.

clue.text: See 24 down
Patience was soft: a king, I'm changed inside

indicators.note: changed means the letters just before it are put in a new order
inside means these pieces go within the other word

blocks.note: mild means gentle or soft
K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's tolerance was weak, as a monarch admits to a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience looks like a virtue but is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta Patience, the title character is a village dairymaid courted by poets.

clue.text: Wherewith ship's warped: for rice dish not enough

indicators.note: not enough means the word falls short, so its final letter is lost

blocks.note: kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish of rice, fish and eggs

explanation.surface: A sailor explains the ship's equipment while complaining the rice ration is meagre.
explanation.walkthrough: To warp a ship is to haul it along with ropes fixed to anchors, not to bend it out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A kedger is a small anchor dropped ahead and used to haul or warp a vessel into position.

clue.text: You have it and it isn't, like mysteries

definitions.text: You have it and it isn't
definitions.note: a cryptic description of this very puzzle, which the solver holds but has not yet finished

blocks.clueFragment: You have it and it isn't
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the prize crossword in your hands, which is not yet cracked
second meaning: never cleared up or explained

explanation.surface: A riddle about possessing something that is not there, like a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the very crossword the solver is holding, a playful self-reference by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysteries that remain open have never been cleared up or explained, which is the sense here.
